prompt.context: Your client is a ferryboat company that has been approached by a city mayor to bid on a 50-year exclusivity right to service commuters who wish to cross a river. So far there is only one bridge crossing the river and traffic during peak hours is just horrible. Therefore the mayor sees this bid as an easy and cheap way to improve commuters' journey.
prompt.question: What would be your approach to determine how much your client should bid for the 50-year exclusivity right?

clarifying_info.q: What kind of businesses are the factories on the other side of the river?
clarifying_info.a: The factories are in fact steel mills.

clarifying_info.q: Are there other ferry competitors in the market?
clarifying_info.a: There are 3 ferry competitors on the market.

clarifying_info.q: When does the traffic jam occur?
clarifying_info.a: Traffic jam only occurs during weekdays.

exhibits.title: River crossing map and bridge waiting time
exhibits.shows: A map showing the ferry route across the river alongside the existing bridge, with a chart indicating bridge waiting time peaks at 1 hour between 6AM and 10AM, and 50,000 workers commuting to factories on the other side.

framework: Frame as an NPV analysis: the maximum bid equals the NPV of all future cash flows the exclusivity right can generate over 50 years
Revenue analysis: estimate addressable commuter market, willingness to pay (WTP), pricing strategy, demand elasticity, and seasonality effects
Cost analysis: split fixed costs (boat investment, parking, cashiers — sized to peak capacity) from variable costs (fuel/gas, labor — question how variable labor truly is)
Competitive strategy: assess whether client has any strategic advantage over the 3 existing ferry competitors; identify how to build one (marketing, exclusive financing, superior service)

Discount rate selection: determine appropriate rate for transportation/infrastructure industry; factor in risk from steel mill industry decline and potential upside from mayor's plan to attract IT businesses
Sensitivity analysis: test how bid value changes with demand assumptions, discount rate, and competitive dynamics

questions.prompt: How would you estimate the revenue potential of the ferry service?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify the 50,000 workers as the potential market, note that peak demand is weekday 6AM-10AM (2-hour window), estimate market share the ferry can realistically capture (noting that as ferry gains share, bridge congestion falls, reducing the ferry's relative attractiveness — a self-limiting demand effect), consider WTP tied to the 1-hour current bridge waiting time (time savings = value), price elasticity, and seasonality (weekday vs weekend, weather).

questions.prompt: How would you structure the cost side of the NPV?
questions.guidance: Fixed costs are determined by peak capacity (number of boats, dock/parking infrastructure, cashier/ticketing staff). Variable costs include fuel/gas and crew labor — candidate should note that labor may behave more like a fixed cost in practice (shift minimums, union rules). Candidate should distinguish capex (boat purchase) from opex.

questions.prompt: What discount rate would you use and why?
questions.guidance: Candidate should reference the transportation/infrastructure sector cost of capital as a baseline. Key risk adjustment: the steel mills (destination industry) are in a declining sector, which threatens long-term commuter volumes and thus revenue. Partially offsetting this risk is the mayor's stated plan to attract IT businesses to the area. A strong candidate notes that discount rate assumptions could be a major source of differentiation between competing bids.

questions.prompt: How does competitive dynamics affect the bid?
questions.guidance: There are 3 existing ferry competitors. Candidate should assess whether the client has a structural advantage (answer: no apparent advantage). Candidate should then brainstorm how to build one — e.g., superior marketing, favorable financing, better service frequency, or co-investment with the city. The exclusivity right itself is valuable precisely because it eliminates these competitors.

brainstorming.prompt: What factors would affect the long-term risk and sustainability of the ferry revenue stream?

categories.name: Demand risk
ideas: Steel mill industry is declining — commuter volumes may fall over 50-year horizon
Population is stable so no organic growth in commuter base
IT business relocation by mayor could introduce new, higher-paid commuters

categories.name: Competitive risk
ideas: 3 current ferry competitors will be eliminated by exclusivity — reduces near-term risk
No apparent strategic advantage today — must build one post-award
Future bridge capacity expansions by the city could reduce ferry value

categories.name: Operational risk
ideas: Peak capacity sizing is critical — over-sizing raises fixed costs, under-sizing loses customers
Weather and seasonal disruptions to ferry service
Labor cost structure (variable vs fixed distinction)

categories.name: Regulatory/political risk
ideas: 50-year contract with a city — subject to political and regulatory changes
Mayor's IT attraction plan may or may not materialize
Exclusivity right enforcement against new bridge or tunnel projects

recommendation: The maximum bid should equal the NPV of projected ferry cash flows over 50 years, using a discount rate that reflects transportation sector risk adjusted upward for the declining steel mill industry
A conservative approach given the steel mill decline risk is to model a base case with flat commuter volumes and a downside with gradual volume decline, and bid based on the base case NPV
risks: Steel mill industry decline could materially reduce commuter demand within the 50-year window
Discount rate uncertainty is the largest variable in bid valuation — a major source of competitive differentiation
If the city builds additional bridge capacity, the ferry's competitive advantage erodes
next_steps: Commission a demand study to validate the 50,000 worker figure and model demand scenarios
Research steel mill industry outlook and the mayor's IT relocation plan timelines
Benchmark discount rates used by infrastructure/transportation investors in comparable bids
Model NPV sensitivity to key assumptions (market share, WTP, discount rate) to set a bid range
